passage1.text: One of my bad habits is saying "busy" when people ask me how I'm doing. Sometimes it's because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that's what I think I'm supposed to say. That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say. But working long hours doesn't drive better results. Never taking a vacation won't lead to a promotion. So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time? In 2016, researchers from Columbia, Harvard, and Georgetown conducted a study to figure it out. They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influenced by our own beliefs about social mobility. In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing. That's why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there's a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails, and stress, then they're probably a big deal. This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout (精疲力竭). Personally, I'm going to stop saying "busy" when people ask me how I am. It sounds self-righteous (自以为是 的) and sets the wrong tone. Phrases like "I have limited access to email" and "I'll respond as soon as I get back" sound like you're being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off. That's why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back. Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same.

passage2.text: Female employees consistently pay lower airfares than men do for the same flights because they tend to book earlier. We compared the airfare paid by employees in the same position within a company for the same class of travel and used a common statistical technique to account for other factors that might affect differences in airfares. We found that women paid on average $18 less per ticket than their male colleagues. Further investigation allowed us to conclude that this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men, 1.8 days on average. We wanted to determine what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips so we tested a variety of possible explanations, such as women choosing to plan ahead or male frequent travelers being inclined to book late. None of these explained away the gender gap, so we applied data collected from surveys that express consumer preferences that play a central role in economic decisions, such as patience and risk avoidance. We found that only the concept of "negative reciprocity"—in which an employee who feels unfairly treated engages in negative behaviors, such as spending their company's money less carefully-explains these differences. The surveys showed men tend to exhibit more of these negative behaviors than women. This isn't to say that all men engage in these behaviors—or that booking relatively late is a sign of abnormal behavior. It only means that the gender gap disappears when we plug in the negative reciprocity variable. Prior research on negative reciprocity among workers found that it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale (士气) and culture. Our results show another way these negative behaviors can manifest themselves, like in airline bookings, and add to evidence that women are less likely to engage in them. Companies spend significant sums of money on business travel. While that $18 difference per ticket may seem small, it adds up. Our analysis suggests early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year for a large multinational company with 20,000 regular travelers.

paragraphs.A: Earlier this year, scientists warned that one in six animal species could go extinct (灭绝的) due to climate change. Could the same thing happen to our crops and other foodstuffs too?
paragraphs.B: It's clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades. Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist's efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts. By using the genes from resurrection (复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water.
paragraphs.C: But if we can't find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change? Fortunately, there is some good news on this front. Despite alarmist headlines about "foods that are going extinct," there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist.
paragraphs.D: But that doesn't mean it's all good news for future food. We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot. The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation. And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods. "Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted," says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the Us Department of Agriculture's Climate Change Program Office. In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn't mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today.
paragraphs.E: Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too. How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of .warming and the crop in question, but in general, "anything over about 30C is very bad for crops," says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University. For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean ( 大豆) production in the Us show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold (临界点).
paragraphs.F: In the US-the world's largest producer of corn and soybeans-farms can move north to some degree, Schlenker says. But eventually, yields will likely suffer because the soil north of Iowa declines in quality-a legacy of glacial (冰川的) expansion. Other studies, including studies of wheat in India and corn in Africa, also found that there is a threshold above which yields sharply decline: crops can adapt and move, but only to a point. "What's common to all studies is the finding that extreme heat is damaging to crop growth, although exact cutoffs vary by crop,” Schlenker says. "If predictions for the end of the century are true, though, I think a lot of agricultural areas in the US will see significant hits."
paragraphs.G: Under current conditions, about 4% of the world's croplands experience drought in any given year, but by the end of the century those conditions are forecasted to jump to about 18% per year. Some studies indicate that horticulture crops—generally, everything besides staples—may be impacted most severely, largely because they tend to be confined to a smaller geographic area. Researcher Andrew Jarvis and his colleagues found that 80% of coffee-growing zones in Central America and Brazil could become unsuitable by 2050, for example, while climate change will likely have “great impacts” on cocoa (可可粉) production in West Africa. "High quality chocolate will be less available in the future, and if you want it, you'll have to pay a lot more for it," Jarvis says.
paragraphs.H: This means that, for those who can afford it, some foods will simply cost them more in the future. But for poorer people, those same price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets. "The more you reduce, the shorter the supply, and the higher the price will jump," Schlenker says.
paragraphs.I: Another potential climate change-induced problem is our dependence on commodity crops-wheat, soybeans, corn and rice—which currently provide humanity with 75% of its calories, either directly or indirectly through the animals we raise on those crops. Jarvis and his colleagues also found that, over the past five decades, the world has seen an increasing standardisation of diets; the foods we eat globally today are 36% more similar than they were in 1961. While this can be good news for the world's poorest people who now consume more calories, protein and fat than in the past, homogeneity (同一性) and over-dependence on a handful of staples leaves us vulnerable to threats such as drought, disease and pests—all of which are predicted to worsen in many parts of the world as a result of climate change.
paragraphs.J: There are ways we could soften the coming blow to the global food supply, however. Like Farrant's work with resurrection crops, a number of companies, organisations and researchers are aiming to create drought-and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering and conventional breeding. For now, the jury is still out as to how successful those endeavours will be. "The people at Monsanto who I've talked to are much more optimistic that they'll be able to engineer heat-tolerant crops," Schlenker says. "On the other hand, scientists at the USDA who I've spoken with are much more cautious.”
paragraphs.K: Until genetic engineering comes to fruition, other strategies might also help in some places, including applying more fertiliser, implementing better irrigation, using machinery that gets crops out of the field faster or installing storage facilities to delay spoilage. "Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist," Walsh says. "General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes."
paragraphs.L: Finally, diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help. "We've seen profound changes in the last decades in what we eat largely as a result of international trade, and I think that trend toward more diversification will continue," Jarvis says. "Depending on a greater number of plant species creates a more vigorous and less risky food system—and one that provides a broader range of nutritional requirements."

questions.script:
Have you noticed how similar you are to your friends? [1] It may be because your brains operate in harmony with
each other. We know that friends are more likely to be the same age, gender and ethnic background as each other. Now
it seems their brains are alike, too.
Researchers at the University of California scanned the brains of 42 classmates while they watched videos intended to provoke varying responses. Some people might find a romantic scene touching, for instance, while others would feel it was embarrassing.The activity of friends'brains was more similar than that of people who didn't know
each other, particularly in regions involved in attention, emotion and language. This similarity was strong enough that it
could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not. [2] The relationship probably goes two ways.
We are drawn to people who think like us; we then influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain
activity into more closely resembling our own.

Two men who have been best friends for 60 years have just realized they are actually brothers. It's reported
that Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald met in the 6th grade at a school in Hawaii. They have been best friends
ever since, Alan was given away for adoption soon after he was born, and Walter never knew his father. [3] So
recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about their ancestry. Walter was
astonished to find that he matched with website user Robi737.He knew immediately that this was his best friend
Alan, whose friends call him Robi and flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot. [4] The pair were born to the same
mother 15 months apart.

week.

questions.script:
New research from America studies the role that the presence of individuals from different social or racial groups
has in influencing consumers' food choices. [l6] This research found college students were more likely to choose
healthy food in the presence of an observer of a different race, as opposed to an observer from their own race. The same
was true when they were with someone from a different university, compared to someone from their own. Researchers
say this was because participants anticipated more negative judgment from an outsider group. In contrast, they felt less
judged by members of their own group.
In one experiment, participants were offered the choice between candy and fruit as a snack. When in the presence
of an unknown student from their own university, only 12 per cent of students selected the healthier option
[17] However, this number was 31 per cent when in the presence of an unknown student from another university. Other
experiments showed similar results based on racial group.
What's the reason for this pattern? The study found that people feel judged to a larger extent by members of other
groups. Because of this, they strategically use healthy food choices to make a positive impression. There have been many
attempts to help consumers make healthier choices, but consumers often struggle to maintain a healthy diet. [18] This
research finds that one way to promote a healthy diet could be to advertise the social benefits of healthy choices.

questions.script:
[19] For college students under pressure, a dog may be the best stress fighter around, according to the finding of
a recent study."It's a really powerful finding," said Patricia Pendry, who led the study."Universities are doing a lot of
great work trying to help students succeed academically, especially those who may be at risk due to a history of mental
health issues or academic and learning issues. [19] This study shows that traditional stress management approaches
aren't as effective for this population compared with programs that focus on providing opportunities to interact with
therapy dogs."
[2o] The researchers measured executive functioning in the students involved in the study. Executive function
is a term for the skills one needs to plan, organize, motivate, concentrate and memorize. These are skills students
need to succeed in college. The researchers found that students who were most at risk had the most improvements in
executive functioning after interacting with therapy dogs. These results remained when researchers followed up six
weeks later.
Many universities provide academic stress management programs and workshops. These are traditionally
very similar to college classes. They often talk about ways to get more sleep, set goals, or manage stress or anxiety.
[2i] Pendry acknowledges that these are really important topics and these workshops help typical students succeed.
But they're less helpful for struggling students. Pendry believes those students may experience the programs as another
lecture and feel even more stressed.

questions.script:
[22] Taking risks in business does not mean going into business blindly and then expecting great results. On the
contrary, taking risks in entrepreneurship involves careful planning and hard work. Nobody can really be sure if risks
will be met with success, no matter how calculated they may be. But this should not stop you from taking risks, as risks
are necessary if you want your business to succeed.
Some risks may not work out, but an optimistic risk-taker will always look at failure as an opportunity to learn.
[23] The willingness to experiment with new ideas is key to business growth. As the old saying goes, Nothing
ventured, nothing gained." Failure will teach you how to think and plan strategically.[24] But just remember that not
all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and move forward.
[25] Since most people tend to avoid risk, businesses that are brave enough to take risks already have a
competitive advantage. They are the ones setting the standard with new ideas, fresh offers and bold inventions. Risk-
takers are best at adapting in difficult times.[25] Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less
competition for risk-takers. We don't know if you'll achieve what these risk-takers have achieved. But for as long as
you want to stay safe, and for as long as you are content with where your business is right now, you will never find out.

Some risks may not work out, but an optimistic risk-taker will always look at failure as an opportunity to learn.
[23] The willingness to experiment with new ideas is key to business growth. As the old saying goes, Nothing
ventured, nothing gained." Failure will teach you how to think and plan strategically.[24] But just remember that not
all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and move forward.
[25] Since most people tend to avoid risk, businesses that are brave enough to take risks already have a
competitive advantage. They are the ones setting the standard with new ideas, fresh offers and bold inventions. Risk-
takers are best at adapting in difficult times.[25] Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less
competition for risk-takers. We don't know if you'll achieve what these risk-takers have achieved. But for as long as
you want to stay safe, and for as long as you are content with where your business is right now, you will never find out.
questions.expl: 详解：文章提到“大多数人规避风险时，勇于承担风险的企业竞争会减少”。A项（更新的提议）是风险企业的做法而非结果；B项（更安全的运作）、C项（更多挑战）均未提及，故排除。 涉及知识点：因果关系定位，捕捉“most people tend to avoid risk”带来的结果。 Part III Reading Comprehension Section A 选词填空

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.expl: impact 详解：语法判断：空格前为“have a meaningful”，后为“on health”，需填名词。语义判断：“短时间低强度运动对健康有重要影响”，“impact on”为固定搭配，符合句意。 涉及知识点：固定搭配“impact on”，词性辨析（名词）。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：空格前为“It's also somewhat”，后为逗号，需填形容词作表语。语义判断：前文说“每周10分钟锻炼延长寿命”的想法新颖，后文提到联邦指南建议更长时间锻炼，前后转折，“有争议的”符合句意。 涉及知识点：语义逻辑（转折），形容词作表语。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.expl: moderate 详解：语法判断：空格前为“150 minutes of”，后为“exercise”，需填形容词修饰名词。语义判断：“联邦指南建议75分钟剧烈运动或150分钟适度运动”，“moderate exercise”为“适度运动”，符合句意。 涉及知识点：并列结构（vigorous与moderate对应），形容词修饰名词。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：空格所在从句缺少谓语，主语为“more than 88,000 U.S. adults”，主句为过去时，需填动词过去式，且能与“in”搭配。语义判断：“参与全国健康访谈调查”，“participated in”为固定搭配，符合句意。 涉及知识点：固定搭配“participate in”，动词时态（过去时）。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.expl: upper 详解：语法判断：空格前为“an”，后为“limit”，需填形容词修饰名词。语义判断：后文说“运动对长寿的好处没有上限”，前后转折，前文指“一些研究发现健康运动量有上限”，“upper limit”为“上限”，符合句意。 涉及知识点：语义逻辑（转折），固定搭配“upper limit”。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.expl: seemingly 详解：语法判断：空格所在句结构完整，需填副词修饰形容词“no”。语义判断：“运动对长寿的好处似乎没有上限”，“seemingly”（似乎）符合句意。 涉及知识点：副词修饰形容词，语义语境理解。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.expl: risk 详解：语法判断：空格前为“had a 46% lower”，后为“of death”，需填名词。语义判断：“运动量是建议值10倍的人群，死亡风险比最不活跃人群低46%”，“risk of death”为“死亡风险”，符合句意。 涉及知识点：固定搭配“risk of”，名词作宾语。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.expl: patterns 详解：语法判断：空格前为“find”，需填名词作宾语。语义判断：“观察性研究不能证明因果关系，只能发现规律”，“patterns”此处译为“规律”，符合句意。 涉及知识点：语义转换（patterns译为“规律”），名词作宾语。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.expl: adjust 详解：语法判断：空格前为“were not able to”，后为“for certain lifestyle factors”，需填动词原形。语义判断：“研究人员无法调整某些影响寿命的生活方式因素”，“adjust for”为“调整以适应”，符合句意。 涉及知识点：固定搭配“adjust for”，动词原形用法。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：空格前为“Despite these”，后为逗号，需填名词复数。语义判断：前文提到观察性研究的不足（不能证明因果、无法调整因素），“limitations”（局限性）符合句意。 涉及知识点：语义指代（these指代前文研究的不足），名词复数形式。 Section B 匹配题

questions.stem: 36. One consequence of climate change is that some people may not have adequate access to certain foods.
questions.expl: 题干“气候变化的一个后果是有些人可能无法充分获得某些食物”对应D段：“气候变暖可能改变农作物种植地点，导致当地人难以像以前一样获得某些食物”。题干中“One consequence of climate change”对应原文“The disadvantage”，“not have adequate access to certain foods”对应“struggle to get the same access to certain foods”。 涉及知识点：同义转述，因果关系匹配。

questions.stem: 37. People around the world are eating foods more similar than what they used to eat.
questions.expl: 题干“世界各地的人们现在吃的食物比过去更相似”对应I段：“过去50年饮食越来越标准化，与1961年相比，全球食物相似度提高36%”。题干中“People around the world”对应“the world”，“more similar than what they used to eat”对应“36% more similar than they were in 1961”。 涉及知识点：语义概括，数字信息转换。

questions.stem: 38. A recent news report talked about scientific efforts to help crops survive droughts through genetic engineering.
questions.expl: 题干“最近的新闻报道谈到通过基因工程帮助农作物在干旱中存活的科学努力”对应B段：“BBC Future探究科学家的努力，通过复活植物的基因设计耐旱农作物”。题干中“A recent news report”对应“Last week, BBC Future”，“scientific efforts to help crops survive droughts”对应“efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts”，“through genetic engineering”对应“By using the genes from resurrection plants”。 涉及知识点：细节匹配，科技类词汇对应（genetic engineering与genes）。

questions.stem: 39. It is predicted that climate change will affect the availability and price of quality chocolate.
questions.expl: 题干“气候变化将影响优质巧克力的供应和价格”对应G段：“气候变化对西非可可粉生产有巨大影响，未来优质巧克力供应减少、价格上涨”。题干中“affect the availability and price of quality chocolate”对应“will be less available... have to pay a lot more”。 涉及知识点：因果关系推导（可可粉是巧克力原料，其生产受影响→巧克力供应和价格受影响）。

questions.stem: 40. People wonder if certain crops and foodstuffs could disappear like some animal species due to climate change.
questions.expl: 题干“人们想知道某些农作物和食物是否会像某些动物物种一样因气候变化而消失”对应A段：“科学家警告六分之一动物物种可能因气候变化灭绝，疑问农作物和其他食物是否会如此”。题干中“People wonder if”对应原文设问句“Could the same thing... too?”，“disappear”对应“go extinct”。 涉及知识点：设问句与陈述句转换，语义对应。

questions.stem: 41. Although farms in the US can move a bit northward, crop yields may decrease.
questions.expl: 题干“尽管美国的农场可以稍微向北迁移，但农作物的产量可能会下降”对应F段：“美国农场可向北迁移，但土壤质量下降导致产量可能受影响”。题干中“farms in the US can move a bit northward”对应“can move north to some degree”，“cropyields may decrease”对应“yields will likely suffer”。 涉及知识点：转折关系匹配，同义替换。

questions.stem: 42. One possible solution to the food security problem is diversification of diet.
questions.expl: 题干“应对粮食安全问题的一个可能的解决办法是饮食多样化”对应L段：“饮食多样化，远离热敏感作物，有助于应对粮食问题”。题干中“One possible solution”对应“could also help”，“diversification of diet”对应“diversifying our diet”。 涉及知识点：解决办法定位，名词与动名词转换。

questions.stem: 43. It remains unsettled whether the global food supply problem can be solved by creating heat-tolerant crops through genetic engineering.
questions.expl: 题干“全球粮食供应问题能否通过基因工程培育出耐热农作物来解决，目前尚无定论”对应J段：“许多机构致力于通过基因工程培育耐旱耐高温农作物，但这些努力能否成功尚无定论”。题干中“It remains unsettled”对应“the jury is still out”，“creating heat-tolerant crops through genetic engineering”对应“create drought- and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering”。 涉及知识点：同义替换，科技类话题匹配。

questions.stem: 44. Poor people may have to give up eating certain foods because of their high prices.
questions.expl: 题干“穷人可能因为高定价而不得不放弃吃某些食物”对应H段：“穷人面临食物价格上涨，某些食物可能从他们的饮食中消失”。题干中“Poor people”对应“poorer people”，“give up eating certain foods because of their high prices”对应“price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets”。 涉及知识点：语义转换，“go extinct from their diets”译为“放弃吃某些食物”。

questions.stem: 45. A number of existing farming technologies could be used to reduce the negative effect of climate change on food production.
questions.expl: 题干“一些现有的农业技术可以被用来减少气候变化对粮食生产的负面影响”对应K段：“在基因工程成功前，施用肥料、改善灌溉等现有技术可以帮助减少气候变化的影响”。题干中“existing farming technologies”对应“technologies that already exist”，“reduce the negative effect of climate change on food production”对应“help in some places”“easing changes”。 涉及知识点：细节概括，捕捉列举的现有技术及其作用。 Section C 阅读理解 Passage One

questions.stem: 46. What is a reason for the author to be in the habit of saying "busy" when asked how he is doing?

options.A: He just follows successful people's example.
options.B: He is actually proud to be fully occupied.
options.C: He thinks everyone should be devoted to work.
options.D: He believes busyness ensures accomplishments.

questions.expl: 详解：定位第一段，作者说“有时回答‘忙’是因为觉得应该这么说，重要人物、升职的人都这么回答”，即效仿成功人士。B项（为忙碌自豪）错误，原文是“觉得应该说”而非“自豪”；C项（认为每个人应投身工作）未提及；D项（相信忙碌确保成就）错误，原文说“长时间工作不能带来更好结果”，故排除。 涉及知识点：细节理解，区分“表面原因”与“深层动机”。

questions.stem: 47. Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status?

options.A: Our status can be attributed to our social mobility.
options.B: We hold the belief that hard work leads to success.
options.C: Our own opportunity for success never comes easily.
options.D: We find few people of high status have time for leisure.

questions.expl: We hold the belief that hard work leads to success. 详解：定位第二段，“我们越是相信努力工作能获得成功，就越认为不休息、一直工作的人地位更高”。A项（地位归因于社会流动性）错误，原文是“地位归属受社会流动看法影响”；C项（成功机会来之不易）未提及；D项（高地位的人很少有休闲时间）未提及，故排除。 涉及知识点：逻辑关系理解，“the more... the more...”引导的因果逻辑。

questions.stem: 48. What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study?

options.A: It places employees in endless meetings, emails and stress.
options.B: It compels some 20% of employees to appear always busy.
options.C: It distorts many employees' belief of what a satisfying life is.
options.D: It does much harm to many busy employees' well-being.

questions.expl: It does much harm to many busy employees' well-being. 详解：定位第三段，“忙碌文化让员工难以平衡工作与生活，每五名高度投入工作的员工就有一人面临精疲力竭的风险”，即损害健康。A项（让员工陷入无休止会议等）是忙碌的表现而非研究发现；B项（迫使20%员工显得忙碌）错误，是“1/5员工有精疲力竭风险”；C项（扭曲对满意生活的信念）未提及，故排除。 涉及知识点：语义概括，“burnout”译为“精疲力竭”，对应“harm to well-being”。

questions.stem: 49. What do such utterances as “I have limited access to email” sound like according to the author?

options.A: One is too busy to check all emails in time.
options.B: One is opposed to the prevailing work culture.
options.C: One is forced by circumstances to stop working.
options.D: One is simply enjoying their time off work.

questions.expl: 详解：定位倒数第二段，“‘我不方便查阅电子邮件’听起来像是不得不停止工作，而不是想充分利用休息时间”。A项（太忙无法及时查邮件）未提及；B项（反对主流工作文化）未提及；D项（享受不工作的时间）与原文矛盾，故排除。 涉及知识点：语义辨析，区分“不得不停止”与“主动享受”。

questions.stem: 50. Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator?

options.A: To enable busy employees to spend less time checking emails.
options.B: To ensure employees as well as employers truly have time off.
options.C: To stop managers from talking about how busy their teams usually are.
options.D: To encourage both employers and employees to answer emails promptly.

questions.expl: To ensure employees as well as employers truly have time off. 详解：定位最后一段，“推出‘外出电子邮件生成器’，让人们可以自豪地说休假期间不查邮件，建议经理周末不发邮件、领导休假并鼓励员工休假”，核心是确保大家真正有休假时间。A项（减少查邮件时间）未提及；C项（阻止经理谈论团队忙碌）错误，是“经理需再三考虑”；D项（鼓励及时回复邮件）与原文矛盾，故排除。 涉及知识点：主旨理解，提炼工具推出的核心目的。 Passage Two

questions.stem: 51. What did the author's team conclude about the gender difference in airfares from their further investigation?

options.A: It is largely attributed to women booking earlier than men.
options.B: It is largely explained by women's choosing cheaper flights.
options.C: It is mainly accounted for by male employees' readiness to pay more.
options.D: It is due to the fact that women care more about their company's money.

questions.expl: 详解：定位第二段，“进一步调查得出结论，机票价格差距主要原因是女性比男性平均早1.8天预订”。B项（选择更便宜的航班）未提及；C项（男性愿意付更多钱）未提及；D项（女性更在乎公司的钱）是后文提到的“消极互惠”的表现，非调查结论，故排除。 涉及知识点：细节定位，区分“调查结论”与“其他解释”。

questions.stem: 52. What did the researchers want to determine by testing a variety of possible explanations?

options.A: What made male frequent travelers book air tickets late.
options.B: What caused women to plan ahead in booking business trips.
options.C: What motivated women to book cheaper flights.
options.D: What accounted for the gender gap in airfares.

questions.expl: What accounted for the gender gap in airfares. 详解：定位第三段，“我们想确定是什么造成了预订商务行程的性别差异，所以测试了各种可能的解释”，此处“性别差异”指机票价格的性别差异。A项（男性频繁旅行者晚预订的原因）、B项（女性提前计划的原因）、C项（女性预订便宜航班的动机）均是测试的具体解释而非目的，故排除。 涉及知识点：主旨定位，区分“研究目的”与“研究手段”。

questions.stem: 53. What happened when the negative reciprocity variable was taken into account?

options.A: Both men and women were found to engage in negative behaviors.
options.B: Neither men nor women viewed booking late as a bad behavior.
options.C: The gender difference in airfare expenses no longer existed.
options.D: The gender gap tended to narrow to a significant degree.

questions.expl: 详解：定位第四段，“当插入消极互惠的变量时，性别差距就消失了”。A项（男女都有负面行为）未提及；B项（均不认为晚预订是不良行为）未提及；D项（性别差距显著缩小）错误，是“消失”而非“缩小”，故排除。 涉及知识点：直接信息提取，“disappears”译为“不复存在”。

questions.stem: 54. What did prior research on negative reciprocity among workers find?

options.A: It can do more harm to the workplace than to employees.
options.B: It contributes to the male-female divide in the workplace.
options.C: It proves to be counterproductive in a number of ways.
options.D: It can result in increasing labor-management conflicts.

questions.expl: 详解：定位第五段，“之前的研究发现消极互惠会导致员工积极性下降、业务绩效降低、工作场所士气和文化低落”，即多方面适得其反。A项（对职场危害比对员工大）未提及；B项（助长职场男女分化）未提及；D项（导致劳资冲突加剧）未提及，故排除。 涉及知识点：语义概括，“counterproductive”（适得其反的）概括多种负面影响。

questions.stem: 55. What does the author emphasize about their analysis in the last paragraph?

options.A: It can help companies increase their savings significantly.
options.B: It can duly contribute to companies’ business performance.
options.C: It can translate women's booking practice into men's behavior.
options.D: It can enhance large multinational companies' competitiveness.

questions.expl: 详解：定位最后一段，“对于有2万名经常出差员工的大型跨国公司，女性提前预订机票每年可节省100万美元”，即帮助公司大幅节约。B项（对业务绩效有贡献）未提及；C项（将女性预订行为转化为男性的）未提及；D项（增强大型跨国公司竞争力）未提及，故排除。 涉及知识点：数字信息解读，“add up”（积少成多）对应“increase their savings significantly”。
